rounds.text: Shilpa Medicare Ltd is demonstrating explosive fundamental acceleration, highlighted by a trailing twelve-month compounded sales growth of 28% [E17] and a staggering 117% compounded profit growth over the same period [E21]. This exceptional operational momentum is further reinforced by recent quarterly performance, showing sales surging 45% YoY and net profit climbing 115% YoY [E66, E68]. Profitability is structurally expanding, with operating margins reaching 28% in the TTM period, marking a significant seven percentage point improvement over three years [E30]. Cash generation backs these earnings robustly, as operating cash flow reached Rs 342 Cr in March 2026, achieving a healthy 1.41x cash conversion rate where profits are fully backed by cash [E34, E35]. Institutional confidence is surging in tandem with these results, evidenced by domestic institutions expanding their stake from 0.06% in December 2023 to 8.26% by September 2026 alongside positive money flow [E44, E45]. Conceded: the valuation is elevated with a P/E of 69.7x and a negative free cash flow of Rs -28 Cr in March 2026 [E1, E36].

The valuation placed on Shilpa Medicare Ltd is detached from its historical financial reality, trading at an aggressive P/E ratio of 69.7x [E1] and an EV/EBITDA of 39.47x against a sector benchmark of 17.13x [E11]. This expensive pricing leaves no margin of safety, as a discounted cash flow analysis puts intrinsic value at Rs 575 per share compared to the market price of Rs 1,014 [E46], resulting in a severe -76.2% margin of safety [E47]. Furthermore, a reverse DCF indicates that today's price already demands a lofty 24.9% earnings growth, significantly above the 17.0% assumed in the base case [E48]. Compounding these valuation concerns, insiders are de-risking as promoters have reduced their stake by 9.88 percentage points from 50.01% down to 40.13% [E42]. Operational performance also fails to justify these multiples, highlighted by a poor 5-year median return on equity of just 4% [E27] and an unremarkable 3-year median ROE of 5% [E28]. Conceded: the company demonstrates strong TTM sales growth of 28% [E17] alongside an impressive 117% TTM profit growth [E21] and solid operating cash flow backing of 93% of operating profit [E37].

Conceded: [E1], [E11], [E46], [E47], [E48], [E27], and [E28]. While those historical ROE figures and DCF models look tight, they entirely ignore the explosive inflection currently underway where TTM profit growth has surged 117% [E21] and sales have jumped 28% [E17], backed by strong cash conversion of 1.41x and Rs 342 Cr in operating cash flow [E34, E35]. The massive surge in institutional conviction—with foreign holdings up 3.59 percentage points and domestic institutions jumping 8.20 percentage points [E43, E44]—proves that professional money recognizes this structural turnaround long before old trailing metrics catch up. Furthermore, operating margins have expanded by 7 percentage points to 28% over three years [E30], riding directly on a powerful sector tailwind score of +0.84 to +0.85 [E73, E75]. Finally, the chart reflects this fundamental acceleration rather than pure speculation, holding a maximum relative-strength rating of 100 [E52] while trading comfortably above both its 50-day and 200-day moving averages [E51].

Conceded: [E21], [E17], [E34], and [E35]. However, pointing to explosive trailing numbers ignores the warning that today's price already implies a staggering 24.9% earnings growth against a base case of only 17.0% [E48]. Furthermore, the valuation is completely detached from reality, trading at a P/E of 69.7x [E1] and EV/EBITDA of 39.47x versus sector benchmarks of 32.16x and 17.13x respectively [E6, E11]. The DCF model confirms an overvaluation of -76.2% with an intrinsic value of Rs 575 against a market price of Rs 1,014 [E46, E47]. While institutional inflows have increased [E43, E44], promoters have dumped their stake by 9.88 percentage points down to 40.13% [E42], signaling a lack of insider alignment during this price-led surge where expectations have outrun delivery [E58]. Finally, the reliance on recent momentum is fragile given that historical performance shows a poor 3-year median ROE of 5% [E28], 5-year median ROE of 4% [E27], and a severe historical drawdown of -72.9% [E54].
